problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $x=e.$ Given that the point $P(e,2,3)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{{e}^{y}}{x}$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$

feedback.problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $y=\pi .$ Given that the point $P$ with $x$-coordinate $1$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=(x+y){e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)}$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=\pi .$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point where $x=1$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(1,\pi ).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(1,\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,\pi ) & =(1+\pi ){e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)} \\  & =(1+\pi ){e}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1+\pi }{e}\end{aligned}
$$
